Analysis: Hypothesis 1 is more focused in its narrative, proposing a direct pathway whereby lithocholic acid (LCA) activates TGR5 on tumor-associated macrophages to repolarize them toward an anti-tumor phenotype in a breast cancer context. This concept, though requiring further quantitative validation and mechanistic clarification, is more straightforwardly testable and could be refined using nanotechnology-based delivery systems and omics techniques. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 links a high-fat diet through gut microbiota dysbiosis to epigenetic changes driving a cancer stem cell phenotype in colorectal cancer. While innovative, it is more complex, involving multiple steps with overlapping pathways and potential confounders. This complexity might reduce its testability and raise safety concerns regarding off-target epigenetic modifications. Overall, Hypothesis 1 offers greater plausibility and testability with a clearer experimental roadmap and more manageable safety profile.
